title: Franz Jackson's arrangement for two basses
summary: Franz Jackson wrote a number for two basses and Jackson and Hinton played it together, Hinton on three-quarter bass and Jackson on the big bass.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Do you remember, Butter Brother, when Franz Francis Jackson came in?
Oh, yeah. Franz Francis Jackson came into the band to play tenor.
Tenor saxophone player?
That's right. He came in and he wrote this thing for bass only.
Yeah.
And you had these guys come up, you know, and they tried it over with you. So one day I asked you,--
It was written for two basses.

Yeah, uh-huh. -- so I asked you, I said, "Milt," I said, "let me try this with you." So Milt looked at me and he said, "All right," you know, and said, you know -- so I went up there and we had a ball.
We played beautifully.

Milt went all over the theater saying, "Do you know one thing?" He said, "John and all them bass players, come up here, man, and try to play this thing. And, Buddy, come up here, man, and no trouble."
We played it right away. We played it, too.
We played it on the job --
Sure, we played it --
-- when we had both basses.
Sure did.
You had your three-quarter bass out there.
That's right.
That was a beautiful bass, that three-quarter size that you had.
Yeah. I still have it.
And I played the big bass. You know, we did it in the Sherman Hotel.
Right.
We did.
That's right.
We used to do it. We'd bring out the bass out there.
That's right.
It was a good arrangement. It was a very, very good arrangement, I thought, you know. Francis Jackson was something else. Later on he had a band in Chicago himself.
Right. I think he still has.
He came from Earl's band, didn't he?
Yes.
Uh-huh.
